units.rawText: <color=orange>I am Atropos. I listen to the wishes of the living and arrange their burials. The kin of the dead shed tears for them, but I cannot shed tears. I destroyed my eyeballs.</color>
units.displayText: I am Atropos. I listen to the wishes of the living and arrange their burials. The kin of the dead shed tears for them, but I cannot shed tears. I destroyed my eyeballs.

spans.text: What about Mortician-2?

units.rawText: She absorbed too many negative emotions during deathbed consolations, which made her think her suffering was real.

units.rawText: <color=orange>I am Lachesis. The wails of the dying echo in my memory. The voices of the dead are frozen in the moment of their passing, and I cannot stop hearing them.</color>

units.rawText: Then we have Mortician-3. The three of them were designed to see each other as sisters, and so we thought she would be affected by her elder sisters' problems. However, she seems stable for now.

units.rawText: <color=orange>Because death ultimately comes for us all, there is no point in delving into its details.</color>

units.rawText: <color=orange>I am Albert. My car exploded, and it severed my leg. Shrapnel cut my neck open, and my life is leaving me.</color>
units.displayText: I am Albert. My car exploded, and it severed my leg. Shrapnel cut my neck open, and my life is leaving me.

spans.text: I am Albert. My car exploded, and it severed my leg. Shrapnel cut my neck open, and my life is leaving me.

units.rawText: Hey, Chief, please don't mess around with our appraisals! A Doll like her could develop problems at any moment; we're better off scrapping her ASAP!

units.rawText: Aren't there a lot of places where fighting is going on? Those places with regional militias that can't afford military A-Dolls are at least still willing to pay out a sum to take care of all the corpses they handle.

units.rawText: They won't get sick, and their family members won't complain. There's also no need for bedside comfort on the battlefield. One Doll can take care of all their problems. We call that a "consumption upgrade".
